pages.text: Back to HomeFrequently Asked QuestionsPractical questions, clearly answered.If anything is unclear, send an enquiry and I can confirm whether I can help.Which curricula and subjects do you support?I support IB Diploma Biology, Chemistry and Environmental Systems and Societies; IB MYP Science; GCSE & IGCSE Biology and Chemistry, including the Biology and Chemistry components of Combined or Coordinated Science; AS & A-Level Biology; and Ontario secondary science. If your course is not listed, send the examination board or programme with your enquiry and I can confirm whether I can help.Subjects & ProgrammesWhat does an online session involve?Sessions are live and one-to-one. The student will be answering questions, explaining their thinking and working through problems rather than just listening. I adjust the explanation and level of support as needed. Lesson documents and resources are shared through Google Drive or our agreed communication method.Online sessionsHow are sessions scheduled across time zones?Sessions are arranged by appointment around the student’s time zone. When you enquire, send your country, time zone and preferred times. I will confirm the agreed local time and account for daylight-saving changes when they affect the schedule.How often should sessions take place?There is no single schedule that suits every student. Some benefit from regular weekly support; others need extra help around a particular assessment or period of the course. We will look at the student’s goals, current understanding, independent study and available time and decide what is useful.What should a student prepare?Whenever possible, tell me at least 48 hours before the session what you want to focus on. Send questions and any school materials through our agreed contact method or shared Google Drive folder in advance. If you have nothing specific to send, I can prepare suitable resources.How are progress updates shared?I discuss lesson priorities, progress and next steps with students and, where appropriate, parents or guardians through our agreed communication method. Updates are adapted to the student and family rather than following a fixed reporting schedule. You are welcome to contact me with questions, and I normally reply within 24 hours on business days, excluding Canadian statutory holidays.How do payments and missed sessions work?Regular tutoring is prepaid in agreed blocks. Payment for a new block is due before the first lesson requiring that block, unless a different date is explicitly agreed. Your rate, currency and any separately charged marking or feedback will be confirmed in advance. Payment can be made by PayPal or bank transfer. Existing client agreements remain in effect. With at least 7 days’ notice, a session can be cancelled without charge. With at least 12 hours’ notice but less than 7 days, it can be rescheduled; the replacement must take place within four weeks of the original date, subject to mutually convenient availability. An unused replacement expires after those four weeks. Cancellations with less than 12 hours’ notice and no-shows normally incur the full session fee. Existing client agreements and any exceptions expressly agreed with Amanda remain in effect.Tutoring policiesWhat guidance is available for assessed work?I can help a student understand an assessed task, ask questions that move their thinking forward and point out places where their reasoning or communication is unclear. The student makes the decisions and produces the final work. I do not write, rewrite or complete assessed work for them.Academic integrity policyThe next stepLet’s talk about the next step.Tell me about the course, learning goals and where support would help. pages.text: Back to HomeAbout AuxesisWhy Auxesis exists.I founded Auxesis Education to help students make progress in science and become more capable, rather than more dependent on tutoring. I support their academic goals while helping them tackle the challenges in front of them.The nameAuxesis means growth.Education is, at its heart, about growth. Not simply acquiring knowledge or achieving a particular grade, but developing the understanding, skills, confidence and independence to keep learning.Growth looks different for every student. For one, it might mean building the foundations needed to move from struggling to succeeding. For another, it might mean moving from meeting expectations to exceeding them. Sometimes the most important progress is less immediately visible: asking a better question, making a connection between ideas, challenging an assumption or approaching an unfamiliar problem with confidence.At Auxesis Education, I believe learning should be active, purposeful and increasingly independent. Students should not simply memorise scientific facts or follow procedures without understanding why they work. They should learn to think critically, explore evidence, recognise patterns, apply knowledge in new situations and develop the confidence to question what they encounter.That philosophy shapes how I facilitate learning. Rather than simply providing answers or delivering information, I create opportunities for students to question, investigate, make connections and construct their own understanding. I meet learners where they are, providing appropriate guidance, challenge and support while gradually encouraging greater independence. The aim is not to remove every difficulty, but to help students develop the confidence, curiosity and skills to navigate challenges themselves.Growth is not always linear, and it cannot always be measured by a grade. Progress can involve uncertainty, mistakes, revisiting old ideas and discovering new ways of thinking. These experiences are not obstacles to learning; they are often an essential part of it.Ultimately, Auxesis is about more than helping students succeed in their next examination. It is about helping them become curious, capable and reflective learners who understand not only what they know, but how to continue learning.The real value of education is not just what students achieve today, but what they become capable of tomorrow.What that looks like in practiceI ask questions and observe how a student approaches problems to identify misconceptions, missing foundations and difficulties applying knowledge. I adjust the pace, prompts and practice to their needs while keeping expectations high.I check understanding by asking students to explain ideas in their own words, recognise when they apply and use them in unfamiliar situations. Their responses help me decide what to address next.High expectations and strong supportMistakes are useful because they show us where to look next.I maintain high expectations while making it safe to ask questions and acknowledge uncertainty. I give constructive feedback and adjust support, from breaking a problem into smaller steps to allowing more time to work through it. Mistakes show me what to address next.I facilitate learning and provide guidance; students take an active part in sessions and practise between them. Parents can support routines and preparation.About AmandaHow Tutoring WorksThe next stepLet’s talk about the next step.Tell me about the course, learning goals and where support would help. From molecular structures and cell organization to classification and evolutionary relationships, I use interactive models, visual comparisons and scientific evidence to help students recognize patterns and connections. Together, we develop the analytical skills needed to interpret unfamiliar biological examples, compare organisms and construct precise, evidence-based examination responses.Form and FunctionUnderstanding the relationship between biological structure and function is central to IB Biology. Students explore how molecular structures, cell organization and specialized tissues enable living systems to function. Through interactive visualizations and guided analysis, I help students connect structures with their biological roles, interpret unfamiliar diagrams and apply these principles to challenging examination questions. A common difficulty is explaining how a particular structure makes a process possible, rather than identifying its parts. We use labelled diagrams and questions to build the connection step by step.Interaction and InterdependenceDiscover the intricate relationships that connect organisms, biological systems and their environments. From cellular communication and physiological regulation to ecological interactions and energy flow, I help students decode complex biological processes through visual simulations, interconnected models and real-world examples. We develop the scientific reasoning needed to interpret experimental data, explain biological interactions and apply knowledge across multiple levels of organization. When a pathway feels like a collection of disconnected steps, we trace the inputs, changes and outputs together before applying the model to an unfamiliar example.Continuity and ChangeUnravel the mechanisms that maintain life across generations while driving biological change. From DNA replication and inheritance to natural selection, evolution and biodiversity, I guide students through the molecular and evolutionary processes that shape living systems. Using genetic models, data analysis and structured problem-solving, we transform abstract concepts into clear scientific explanations, building the precision needed to evaluate evidence and tackle challenging IB examination questions.Understanding and examination techniqueWe work through unfamiliar diagrams, experimental data and challenging questions, building understanding rather than relying on memorized answers. I also teach students to decode command terms and dissect mark schemes, so they can turn sound biological knowledge into clear, precise examination responses. The aim is greater confidence, stronger scientific reasoning and a deeper understanding of Biology. Lessons use the student’s classroom work and upcoming assessments; we can rebuild foundations or focus on greater precision in applying and communicating ideas.Can you help with a Biology IA or Extended Essay?Yes. I provide ethical guidance for Biology Internal Assessments and Extended Essays, helping students think through questions, methods, analysis and evaluation. The decisions, analysis and final submitted work remain the student’s own.Do you support both SL and HL Biology?Yes. Through interactive models, visual simulations and worked examples, I help students visualize abstract reactions and connect particle-level explanations with observable changes.Topics coveredStructure: models, bonding and materialsWe explore the particulate nature of matter, atomic structure, bonding and the organization of substances. Visual models help students connect electron arrangements and bonding to the properties of materials, while calculations and evidence help them test and communicate their explanations. Students can find it difficult to move between a particle model, a formula and a bulk property; we compare representations and explain the link rather than treating each as a separate fact.Reactivity: energy, rates and chemical changeWe investigate why and how chemical reactions occur, including energy changes, reaction rates and equilibrium, acids and bases, redox and relevant organic reactions. Simulations and worked examples help students connect equations, mechanisms and particle-level models to observations and solve unfamiliar problems. For example, an equilibrium model can help distinguish equal reaction rates from equal concentrations and explain how a system responds to a change in conditions.Calculations, practical work and evidenceWe work through the reasoning behind quantities, units and multi-step calculations, checking whether an answer is chemically sensible. Students also practise interpreting experimental results, evaluating methods and connecting evidence with explanations. Lessons are shaped by the student’s classroom work and the areas where understanding or application is getting in the way.From understanding to examination responsesLessons follow the SL or HL curriculum and develop the confidence to move between equations, models, experimental evidence and scientific explanations. We explore the reasoning behind calculations, reaction mechanisms and unfamiliar problems, rather than simply memorizing procedures. Students learn to interpret command terms, dissect mark schemes and structure answers with precision. We practise with unfamiliar questions, identifying what the question asks, selecting the relevant chemistry and showing a clear chain of reasoning.Building connections across the courseChemical ideas are more useful when students can connect them. If your course is not listed, send the examination board or programme with your enquiry and I can confirm whether I can help.Subjects & ProgrammesWhat does an online session involve?Sessions are live and one-to-one. The student will be answering questions, explaining their thinking and working through problems rather than just listening. I adjust the explanation and level of support as needed. Lesson documents and resources are shared through Google Drive or our agreed communication method.Online sessionsHow are sessions scheduled across time zones?Sessions are arranged by appointment around the student’s time zone. When you enquire, send your country, time zone and preferred times. I will confirm the agreed local time and account for daylight-saving changes when they affect the schedule.How often should sessions take place?There is no single schedule that suits every student. Some benefit from regular weekly support; others need extra help around a particular assessment or period of the course. We will look at the student’s goals, current understanding, independent study and available time and decide what is useful.What should a student prepare?Whenever possible, tell me at least 48 hours before the session what you want to focus on. Send questions and any school materials through our agreed contact method or shared Google Drive folder in advance. If you have nothing specific to send, I can prepare suitable resources.How are progress updates shared?I discuss lesson priorities, progress and next steps with students and, where appropriate, parents or guardians through our agreed communication method. Updates are adapted to the student and family rather than following a fixed reporting schedule. You are welcome to contact me with questions, and I normally reply within 24 hours on business days, excluding Canadian statutory holidays.How do payments and missed sessions work?Regular tutoring is prepaid in agreed blocks. Payment for a new block is due before the first lesson requiring that block, unless a different date is explicitly agreed. Your rate, currency and any separately charged marking or feedback will be confirmed in advance. Payment can be made by PayPal or bank transfer. Existing client agreements remain in effect. With at least 7 days’ notice, a session can be cancelled without charge. With at least 12 hours’ notice but less than 7 days, it can be rescheduled; the replacement must take place within four weeks of the original date, subject to mutually convenient availability. An unused replacement expires after those four weeks. Cancellations with less than 12 hours’ notice and no-shows normally incur the full session fee. Existing client agreements and any exceptions expressly agreed with Amanda remain in effect.Tutoring policiesWhat guidance is available for assessed work?I can help a student understand an assessed task, ask questions that move their thinking forward and point out places where their reasoning or communication is unclear. The student makes the decisions and produces the final work. pages.text: Back to HomeAbout AmandaMore than 25 years in science education.I’m Amanda D’Souza. I have been teaching science for more than 25 years, and my career has taken me through Canada, Japan, Australia, England, Egypt, Barbados, Qatar and Vietnam.AAmanda D’SouzaExperienceCurriculum and leadership experienceOver the years I have taught IB Diploma Biology, Chemistry and Environmental Systems and Societies; IB MYP Science; the International Middle Years Curriculum; GCSE & IGCSE Biology and Chemistry, including Combined and Coordinated Science; AS & A-Level Biology; and Ontario secondary science.I have also led science departments in Vietnam and Barbados and worked in curriculum development, assessment and teacher mentoring.IB Biology assessment experienceSince 2013, I have worked as an IB Biology Assistant Examiner. I continue to examine IB Biology papers and moderate Biology Internal Assessments, and have experience assessing HL Paper 2 against IB criteria. That work has given me a close understanding of how IB assessment criteria are applied and of the difference between knowing the science and communicating that knowledge effectively under assessment conditions.Subjects & ProgrammesQualificationsBiology, education and professional certification.Academic qualificationsBachelor of Science in Biology — University of Western Ontario, London, Ontario (2000)Graduate Diploma in Education — University of Wollongong, New South Wales, Australia (2002)Professional credentialsOntario Certified Teacher (OCT #496538), with Intermediate and Senior qualifications in Biology and ChemistryQualified Teacher Status in EnglandGuidance and Career Education Additional Qualification Parts 1 and 2LinkedIn profileInternational educationI spent about 20 years living and working internationally, teaching students from many backgrounds and working within different school systems. That has given me a broad view of education and shown me something practical: a student can move from one school or curriculum to another and suddenly appear to have “gaps” simply because the sequence, terminology or expectations have changed. pages.text: Back to HomeAbout AuxesisWhy Auxesis exists.I founded Auxesis Education to help students make progress in science and become more capable, rather than more dependent on tutoring. I support their academic goals while helping them tackle the challenges in front of them.The nameAuxesis means growth.Education is, at its heart, about growth. Not simply acquiring knowledge or achieving a particular grade, but developing the understanding, skills, confidence and independence to keep learning.Growth looks different for every student. For one, it might mean building the foundations needed to move from struggling to succeeding. For another, it might mean moving from meeting expectations to exceeding them. Sometimes the most important progress is less immediately visible: asking a better question, making a connection between ideas, challenging an assumption or approaching an unfamiliar problem with confidence.At Auxesis Education, I believe learning should be active, purposeful and increasingly independent. Students should not simply memorise scientific facts or follow procedures without understanding why they work. They should learn to think critically, explore evidence, recognise patterns, apply knowledge in new situations and develop the confidence to question what they encounter.That philosophy shapes how I facilitate learning. Rather than simply providing answers or delivering information, I create opportunities for students to question, investigate, make connections and construct their own understanding. I meet learners where they are, providing appropriate guidance, challenge and support while gradually encouraging greater independence. The aim is not to remove every difficulty, but to help students develop the confidence, curiosity and skills to navigate challenges themselves.Growth is not always linear, and it cannot always be measured by a grade. Progress can involve uncertainty, mistakes, revisiting old ideas and discovering new ways of thinking. These experiences are not obstacles to learning; they are often an essential part of it.Ultimately, Auxesis is about more than helping students succeed in their next examination. It is about helping them become curious, capable and reflective learners who understand not only what they know, but how to continue learning.The real value of education is not just what students achieve today, but what they become capable of tomorrow.What that looks like in practiceI ask questions and observe how a student approaches problems to identify misconceptions, missing foundations and difficulties applying knowledge. I adjust the pace, prompts and practice to their needs while keeping expectations high.I check understanding by asking students to explain ideas in their own words, recognise when they apply and use them in unfamiliar situations. Their responses help me decide what to address next.High expectations and strong supportMistakes are useful because they show us where to look next.I maintain high expectations while making it safe to ask questions and acknowledge uncertainty. I give constructive feedback and adjust support, from breaking a problem into smaller steps to allowing more time to work through it. Students explore how molecular structures, cell organization and specialized tissues enable living systems to function. Through interactive visualizations and guided analysis, I help students connect structures with their biological roles, interpret unfamiliar diagrams and apply these principles to challenging examination questions. The student will be answering questions, explaining their thinking and working through problems rather than just listening. I adjust the explanation and level of support as needed. Lesson documents and resources are shared through Google Drive or our agreed communication method.Online sessionsHow are sessions scheduled across time zones?Sessions are arranged by appointment around the student’s time zone. When you enquire, send your country, time zone and preferred times. I will confirm the agreed local time and account for daylight-saving changes when they affect the schedule.How often should sessions take place?There is no single schedule that suits every student. Some benefit from regular weekly support; others need extra help around a particular assessment or period of the course. We will look at the student’s goals, current understanding, independent study and available time and decide what is useful.What should a student prepare?Whenever possible, tell me at least 48 hours before the session what you want to focus on. Send questions and any school materials through our agreed contact method or shared Google Drive folder in advance. If you have nothing specific to send, I can prepare suitable resources.How are progress updates shared?I discuss lesson priorities, progress and next steps with students and, where appropriate, parents or guardians through our agreed communication method. Updates are adapted to the student and family rather than following a fixed reporting schedule. You are welcome to contact me with questions, and I normally reply within 24 hours on business days, excluding Canadian statutory holidays.How do payments and missed sessions work?Regular tutoring is prepaid in agreed blocks. Payment for a new block is due before the first lesson requiring that block, unless a different date is explicitly agreed. Your rate, currency and any separately charged marking or feedback will be confirmed in advance. Payment can be made by PayPal or bank transfer. Existing client agreements remain in effect. With at least 7 days’ notice, a session can be cancelled without charge. With at least 12 hours’ notice but less than 7 days, it can be rescheduled; the replacement must take place within four weeks of the original date, subject to mutually convenient availability. An unused replacement expires after those four weeks. Cancellations with less than 12 hours’ notice and no-shows normally incur the full session fee. Existing client agreements and any exceptions expressly agreed with Amanda remain in effect.Tutoring policiesWhat guidance is available for assessed work?I can help a student understand an assessed task, ask questions that move their thinking forward and point out places where their reasoning or communication is unclear. pages.text: Back to HomeAbout AuxesisWhy Auxesis exists.I founded Auxesis Education to help students make progress in science and become more capable, rather than more dependent on tutoring. I support their academic goals while helping them tackle the challenges in front of them.The nameAuxesis means growth.Education is, at its heart, about growth. Not simply acquiring knowledge or achieving a particular grade, but developing the understanding, skills, confidence and independence to keep learning.Growth looks different for every student. For one, it might mean building the foundations needed to move from struggling to succeeding. For another, it might mean moving from meeting expectations to exceeding them. Sometimes the most important progress is less immediately visible: asking a better question, making a connection between ideas, challenging an assumption or approaching an unfamiliar problem with confidence.At Auxesis Education, I believe learning should be active, purposeful and increasingly independent. Students should not simply memorise scientific facts or follow procedures without understanding why they work. They should learn to think critically, explore evidence, recognise patterns, apply knowledge in new situations and develop the confidence to question what they encounter.That philosophy shapes how I facilitate learning. Rather than simply providing answers or delivering information, I create opportunities for students to question, investigate, make connections and construct their own understanding. I meet learners where they are, providing appropriate guidance, challenge and support while gradually encouraging greater independence. The aim is not to remove every difficulty, but to help students develop the confidence, curiosity and skills to navigate challenges themselves.Growth is not always linear, and it cannot always be measured by a grade. Progress can involve uncertainty, mistakes, revisiting old ideas and discovering new ways of thinking. These experiences are not obstacles to learning; they are often an essential part of it.Ultimately, Auxesis is about more than helping students succeed in their next examination. It is about helping them become curious, capable and reflective learners who understand not only what they know, but how to continue learning.The real value of education is not just what students achieve today, but what they become capable of tomorrow.What that looks like in practiceI ask questions and observe how a student approaches problems to identify misconceptions, missing foundations and difficulties applying knowledge. I adjust the pace, prompts and practice to their needs while keeping expectations high.I check understanding by asking students to explain ideas in their own words, recognise when they apply and use them in unfamiliar situations. Their responses help me decide what to address next.High expectations and strong supportMistakes are useful because they show us where to look next.I maintain high expectations while making it safe to ask questions and acknowledge uncertainty. I give constructive feedback and adjust support, from breaking a problem into smaller steps to allowing more time to work through it. Mistakes show me what to address next.I facilitate learning and provide guidance; students take an active part in sessions and practise between them. pages.text: Back to HomeTutoring PoliciesClear arrangements make tutoring easier for everyone.Please read through the policies before regular sessions begin and ask if anything is unclear.PaymentRegular tutoring is prepaid in agreed blocks. Payment for a new block is due before the first lesson requiring that block, unless a different date is explicitly agreed. Your rate, currency and any separately charged marking or feedback will be confirmed in advance. Payment can be made by PayPal or bank transfer. Existing client agreements remain in effect.Cancellations and reschedulingWith at least 7 days’ notice, a session can be cancelled without charge. With at least 12 hours’ notice but less than 7 days, it can be rescheduled; the replacement must take place within four weeks of the original date, subject to mutually convenient availability. An unused replacement expires after those four weeks. Cancellations with less than 12 hours’ notice and no-shows normally incur the full session fee. Existing client agreements and any exceptions expressly agreed with Amanda remain in effect.Academic integrityOur role is to guide the student’s thinking without taking over assessed work. We help students understand the task, examine their reasoning and identify areas for further attention, while decisions, analysis and final submitted work remain the student’s own. The work must meet the academic-integrity requirements of their school or examination board.Working togetherTutoring works best when the student is actively involved. I expect students to attempt tasks, answer and ask questions, and tell me when they need help. Parents can support the process with encouragement and practical organisation, while the student remains responsible for their learning. I can provide additional practice when it is useful, but tutoring does not replace school or independent study. I provide honest feedback about the student’s current understanding, the progress they are making and the most useful next steps.The next stepLet’s talk about the next step.Tell me about the course, learning goals and where support would help. It takes about 20 minutes and gives us a chance to discuss the course, needs and goals, ask questions and get a feel for how I work. Parents are welcome to take part. An initial enquiry does not require a separate parent phone call.03Decision and first lessonThere is no pressure to decide during that meeting. Take time to consider it, then contact me if you would like to proceed. I confirm the arrangements and first session date with you, and we decide what to tackle first. The first paid session is a tutoring lesson. I begin with the priorities we have identified and adjust the questions, pace and level of support as I see how the student thinks and what they understand.04Ongoing tutoringFrom there, tutoring develops with the student. Lessons respond to what they need now while continuing to build stronger understanding, exam skills and independence.SMART goals. Clear next steps.Together, we identify areas to strengthen and set specific, manageable goals. We agree on clear next steps and when to review progress, using the student’s work to recognise improvement and decide what to tackle next.How we workLive, one-to-one sessions.Sessions are live and one-to-one on Google Meet. Students explain ideas, answer questions and work through problems with me throughout the session. Most sessions are 60 minutes, although longer sessions can be arranged. Students need a personal Gmail address, a stable internet connection and a computer or tablet with a microphone and camera. Cameras are expected to stay on during tutoring.Lesson documents and resources can be shared through a Google Drive folder and the communication method we agree on. Students should download or copy any resources they want to keep before access ends.Making the sessions usefulI suggest additional practice when it will genuinely support the student’s learning. Practice is the student’s responsibility. If practice is not completed, we simply begin the next session from where the student is.Communication with students and parentsBetween sessions, students can contact me by email or, where arranged, Google Chat. After enrolment, parents may also choose to communicate through WhatsApp; I do not require WhatsApp as part of the tutoring setup. I normally reply within 24 hours on business days, excluding Canadian statutory holidays.Students can send a quick question using our agreed contact method if they get stuck. I can answer a brief question outside a session. Questions requiring a fuller explanation, substantial review or extended support are best addressed during a scheduled session. Extra support can be booked in 30-minute increments when I have availability, and detailed marking or extended feedback can be handled during a session or arranged separately.I discuss what we are working on, how things are progressing and useful next steps with the student and, where appropriate, their parent or guardian. Communication is adapted to the student and family rather than following a fixed reporting schedule.FeesConfirmed before you decide whether to proceed.Send an enquiry with the subject, programme and kind of support you are looking for. pages.text: Back to Subjects & ProgrammesOne-to-one online tutoringOnline IB Biology tutoringMaster IB Biology by connecting the microscopic world of cells and molecules with the physiological processes that sustain life. Using interactive models, visual simulations and carefully chosen examples, I help students make sense of complex biological systems and see how ideas fit together across the SL and HL curriculum.Topics coveredUnity and DiversityExplore the remarkable diversity of life while uncovering the fundamental biological principles that unite living organisms. From molecular structures and cell organization to classification and evolutionary relationships, I use interactive models, visual comparisons and scientific evidence to help students recognize patterns and connections. Together, we develop the analytical skills needed to interpret unfamiliar biological examples, compare organisms and construct precise, evidence-based examination responses.Form and FunctionUnderstanding the relationship between biological structure and function is central to IB Biology. Students explore how molecular structures, cell organization and specialized tissues enable living systems to function. Through interactive visualizations and guided analysis, I help students connect structures with their biological roles, interpret unfamiliar diagrams and apply these principles to challenging examination questions. A common difficulty is explaining how a particular structure makes a process possible, rather than identifying its parts. We use labelled diagrams and questions to build the connection step by step.Interaction and InterdependenceDiscover the intricate relationships that connect organisms, biological systems and their environments. From cellular communication and physiological regulation to ecological interactions and energy flow, I help students decode complex biological processes through visual simulations, interconnected models and real-world examples. We develop the scientific reasoning needed to interpret experimental data, explain biological interactions and apply knowledge across multiple levels of organization. When a pathway feels like a collection of disconnected steps, we trace the inputs, changes and outputs together before applying the model to an unfamiliar example.Continuity and ChangeUnravel the mechanisms that maintain life across generations while driving biological change. From DNA replication and inheritance to natural selection, evolution and biodiversity, I guide students through the molecular and evolutionary processes that shape living systems. Using genetic models, data analysis and structured problem-solving, we transform abstract concepts into clear scientific explanations, building the precision needed to evaluate evidence and tackle challenging IB examination questions.Understanding and examination techniqueWe work through unfamiliar diagrams, experimental data and challenging questions, building understanding rather than relying on memorized answers. I also teach students to decode command terms and dissect mark schemes, so they can turn sound biological knowledge into clear, precise examination responses. The aim is greater confidence, stronger scientific reasoning and a deeper understanding of Biology. pages.text: Back to HomeAbout AuxesisWhy Auxesis exists.I founded Auxesis Education to help students make progress in science and become more capable, rather than more dependent on tutoring. I support their academic goals while helping them tackle the challenges in front of them.The nameAuxesis means growth.Education is, at its heart, about growth. Not simply acquiring knowledge or achieving a particular grade, but developing the understanding, skills, confidence and independence to keep learning.Growth looks different for every student. For one, it might mean building the foundations needed to move from struggling to succeeding. For another, it might mean moving from meeting expectations to exceeding them. Sometimes the most important progress is less immediately visible: asking a better question, making a connection between ideas, challenging an assumption or approaching an unfamiliar problem with confidence.At Auxesis Education, I believe learning should be active, purposeful and increasingly independent. Students should not simply memorise scientific facts or follow procedures without understanding why they work. They should learn to think critically, explore evidence, recognise patterns, apply knowledge in new situations and develop the confidence to question what they encounter.That philosophy shapes how I facilitate learning. Rather than simply providing answers or delivering information, I create opportunities for students to question, investigate, make connections and construct their own understanding. I meet learners where they are, providing appropriate guidance, challenge and support while gradually encouraging greater independence. The aim is not to remove every difficulty, but to help students develop the confidence, curiosity and skills to navigate challenges themselves.Growth is not always linear, and it cannot always be measured by a grade. Progress can involve uncertainty, mistakes, revisiting old ideas and discovering new ways of thinking. These experiences are not obstacles to learning; they are often an essential part of it.Ultimately, Auxesis is about more than helping students succeed in their next examination. It is about helping them become curious, capable and reflective learners who understand not only what they know, but how to continue learning.The real value of education is not just what students achieve today, but what they become capable of tomorrow.What that looks like in practiceI ask questions and observe how a student approaches problems to identify misconceptions, missing foundations and difficulties applying knowledge. I adjust the pace, prompts and practice to their needs while keeping expectations high.I check understanding by asking students to explain ideas in their own words, recognise when they apply and use them in unfamiliar situations. Their responses help me decide what to address next.High expectations and strong supportMistakes are useful because they show us where to look next.I maintain high expectations while making it safe to ask questions and acknowledge uncertainty. I give constructive feedback and adjust support, from breaking a problem into smaller steps to allowing more time to work through it. Mistakes show me what to address next.I facilitate learning and provide guidance; students take an active part in sessions and practise between them. Parents can support routines and preparation.About AmandaHow Tutoring WorksThe next stepLet’s talk about the next step.Tell me about the course, learning goals and where support would help. I expect students to attempt tasks, answer and ask questions, and tell me when they need help. Parents can support the process with encouragement and practical organisation, while the student remains responsible for their learning. I begin with the priorities we have identified and adjust the questions, pace and level of support as I see how the student thinks and what they understand.04Ongoing tutoringFrom there, tutoring develops with the student. Lessons respond to what they need now while continuing to build stronger understanding, exam skills and independence.SMART goals. Clear next steps.Together, we identify areas to strengthen and set specific, manageable goals. Students explain ideas, answer questions and work through problems with me throughout the session. Most sessions are 60 minutes, although longer sessions can be arranged. Students need a personal Gmail address, a stable internet connection and a computer or tablet with a microphone and camera.
